LESSON: READING 6.2.1 READING: FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Reading: Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Reading: Fluency, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to read fluently?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify instances of expressive reading from a reading or digital text,  View a variety of video clips featuring well-read scripts related to the theme. Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing. Why is it important to read fluently? 53

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading: Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read a text at the right speed, accurately and with expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading: Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the importance of reading fluency in communication.  Watch news clips from a favourite television programme/presenter and comment on the presenter’s speed, accuracy, and expression,  Brainstorm ways of reading effectively. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views, allowing more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views.  Reflect on the qualities of a good reader,  Read a text such as a poem, a narrative, or dialogue with: - With appropriate expressions - With accuracy - right speed,  Listen to a text read by a peer and provide feedback,  Engage in a readers’ theatre and read a poem, narrative, or dialogue,  Read a choral verse in pairs or small groups,  Time himself or herself while reading an excerpt of a text, 54  Participate in activities that enhance reading fluently, such as reader’s theatre, paired reading, echo reading, repeated reading and choral reading.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading: Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Reading: Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Learning to learn is developed as the learner builds on own learning experiences by listening and modelling fluent reading.

 Self-efficacy is developed as the learner documents success criteria while timing themselves as they read excerpts in pairs.

 Communication and collaboration is enhanced as the learner recites a choral verse clearly.

Values

Respect is achieved as the learner values human dignity while listening to their peers’ reading.

Values:

with expression.

Link to other subjects

The learner relates the skill of fluency in reading with reading demands in other learning areas where reading fluency is

demanded such as in Kiswahili.
